$description: Structured representation of the nine interaction primitives defined in context/behaviors.md. Non-authoritative — see context/manifest.md §7. Prose rationale lives in the Markdown; this file carries identifiers, enumerations, and relationships only.

capability_to_primitive_mapping.source: behaviors.md, 'Relationship to the Product Ontology'; product.md §2.6

primitives.name: Finding
primitives.purpose: Present what the Operations Agent has observed, compared, or inferred, without asserting more certainty than the evidence supports.
primitives.governance_implications: none on its own; Observe-tier and Permitted by definition
primitives.ontology_note: Not a Core Object of the Product Ontology; findingId is an interaction-layer identifier only (product.md §2.6).
gaps: Rule 003's 'when practical' threshold for exposing evidence is undefined
whether numerical confidence may ever be shown at all is unresolved (product.md §9)

primitives.name: Evidence Inspection
primitives.purpose: Let a human examine the underlying evidence, its quality, and its limitations behind a Finding, Recommendation, Prepared Action, Approval, or Escalation.
human_actions_permitted: request more evidence (-> Correction, or back to agent for further observation)
primitives.governance_implications: none directly; evidence surfaced here justifies Escalation or a Progress hold under Rule 006
gaps: how conflicting sources should be represented is unresolved

primitives.name: Recommendation
primitives.purpose: Suggest a next action without committing to it.
primitives.governance_implications: none on its own; governance attaches once something is Prepared from it
gaps: whether a Recommendation stage is always required before Prepare, or can be compressed for high-urgency safety cases (Scenario 003 appears to skip to Escalation), is unresolved

primitives.name: Prepared Action
primitives.purpose: Present an agent-created artifact or action that is ready for human inspection, editing, routing, authorization, handoff, or execution.
human_actions_permitted: forward to Approval, Escalation, or direct execution if Permitted
primitives.governance_implications: carries no governance decision of its own; can exist under any governance outcome including Prohibited (should not progress) and Escalation Required (carried forward by Escalation rather than Approval)
primitives.ontology_note: Not a Core Object of the Product Ontology; preparedActionId is an interaction-layer identifier only (product.md §2.6).
gaps: which fields must be revalidated per action type under Rule 009 is unresolved generically (product.md §9); identified per-feature only
whether/when a Prepared Action expires if left undecided is unresolved

primitives.name: Approval
primitives.purpose: Provide the governance interaction through which an authorized human permits or rejects execution of a Prepared Action.
primitives.agent_states_note: none directly — a human-authorization event over a Prepared Action, not an agent capability state
human_actions_permitted: edit the linked Prepared Action then approve
primitives.governance_implications: exists precisely when Governance = ApprovalRequired; any authorized actor for that action type may act, not necessarily a specific higher-authority role
primitives.ontology_note: Dual status: also a Core Object of the Product Ontology (product.md §2.2-2.3) — the record and the experience of creating that record, viewed from two angles.
gaps: who counts as an 'authorized human actor' generally is unresolved (full RBAC gap, product.md §9)

primitives.name: Escalation
primitives.purpose: Route a Finding or Prepared Action to a specific role or higher-authority actor, rather than letting the current actor resolve it.
primitives.governance_implications: exists precisely when Governance = EscalationRequired; target role is UNRESOLVED for damage liability and safety authority (product.md §7.4, §9)
gaps: specific roles authorized to receive a damage-liability escalation or a safety escalation are both unresolved (product.md §7.4, §9)

primitives.name: Correction
primitives.purpose: Let an authorized human resolve ambiguity in a Finding — determine what's actually true — rather than merely approving or rejecting a proposed action.
primitives.governance_implications: Correction outcomes can themselves trigger Escalation ('escalate dispute'); the resulting record change may need its own governance treatment not yet resolved (product.md §7.3)
gaps: what happens when evidence remains inconclusive after correction is attempted is unresolved (product.md §9)
what customer dispute process exists is unresolved

primitives.name: Progress
primitives.purpose: Show where a given Agent Action currently sits in its capability/governance lifecycle, and — where required — actively hold up an ordinary workflow until that lifecycle resolves.
primitives.human_actions_note: for a blocking state, the spec defines no override — the human role authorized to lift a hold is UNRESOLVED (product.md §7.4, Scenario 003)
primitives.governance_implications: a blocking Progress state operationalizes Escalation Required or Approval Required as a real constraint on the product, not just a review queue
gaps: relationship between operational availability, safety status, reservation assignment, and maintenance status is unresolved (product.md §2.4), so it is unclear which underlying object states a 'blocked' status should change
no scenario walks through an execution failure; failure-state behavior is a placeholder, not a specified design

primitives.name: Resolution Alternatives
primitives.purpose: When the agent's own behavior introduces friction — a block, delay, or escalation — proactively offer safe ways forward rather than leaving the human with only a stop.
primitives.governance_implications: none defined independently; selecting an alternative may trigger a new Agent Action with its own governance
gaps: 'equivalent equipment' has a scoped definition for Feature 001 only (product.md §7.1); Scenario 003's broader alternative-equipment matching has no defined equivalence rule of its own

cross_cutting_requirements.name: Impact/Urgency disclosure
cross_cutting_requirements.not_a_primitive_because: no distinct interaction shape of its own
cross_cutting_requirements.requirement: Rule 002 requires potential consequence and intervention urgency be represented as two independent values, never collapsed into one severity score.

cross_cutting_requirements.name: Don't invent missing policy
cross_cutting_requirements.not_a_primitive_because: cross-cutting constraint, not an interaction shape
cross_cutting_requirements.requirement: Every primitive must surface an unresolved policy as visibly unresolved rather than have the interface silently default it.

rows.scenario_002: Required (draft damage report, carried forward by Escalation)
rows.scenario_003: Ambiguous — whether a discrete instance also exists for a formal safety hold is unresolved
Not required as specified — outcome likely Escalation, exact mechanism unresolved

rows.scenario_002: Required ('Prepare and Escalate together', manager review)

rows.scenario_001: Not required — human only approves/rejects a drafted message
rows.scenario_002: Required (confirm / mark pre-existing / request evidence / dismiss / escalate dispute)
rows.scenario_003: Partial/underspecified — no defined menu of outcomes
Required (tracks Observe->Blocked->Escalated, including the active hold)

rows.scenario_001: Not required — Feature 001 as approved stops at contacting the renter (gap against Rule 007)
rows.scenario_002: Not required — scenario is about liability determination, not equipment availability
rows.scenario_003: Required (nearby equivalent equipment, transfer time, substitute classes, schedule flexibility, upgrade or delivery alternatives)
